(a) Assessment.—The Secretaries of the military departments shall each conduct an assessment of post-traumatic stress disorder incidence by military occupation, including identification of military occupations with a high incidence of such disorder. 
    (b) Report.—Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretaries shall each submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the assessment under subsection (a). 
    (c) Centers of Excellence.—The Secretary of Defense shall ensure that all studies, findings, plans, and reports conducted or submitted under this section are transmitted to the centers of excellence established by sections 1621 and 1622 of the Wounded Warrior Act (title XVI of Public Law 110–181).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the report requirement and the transmittal to the centers of excellence are consultative processes. But the report goes to congressional committees, and the centers of excellence are Department of Defense entities, so every actor is inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted before any federal decision, and no rulemaking, hearing or right to sue is created.
fable.s: the Secretaries shall each submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the assessment under subsection (a).

opus.w: The military departments do the assessment, report to the congressional defense committees, and send the results to Department of Defense centers of excellence. Every one of these actors is inside the federal government. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue. The reporting and transfer of findings may look procedural, but none of it crosses the federal boundary.
opus.s: the Secretaries shall each submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the assessment under subsection (a).
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The report to the congressional defense committees and the transfer of findings to the "centers of excellence" can look like outside involvement. **Why it fails:** Congress is inside the federal government. The centers of excellence created by the Wounded Warrior Act are Department of Defense entities. Every actor here is federal, and no outside party is consulted before a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretaries of the military departments to conduct an assessment and submit a report to congressional defense committees. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation. The transmission of findings to 'centers of excellence' established by federal statute is also an internal government action. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretaries shall each submit to the congressional defense committees a report on the assessment under subsection (a).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "centers of excellence" are outside entities that receive information, implying coordination. However, these centers are established by federal law (Wounded Warrior Act) and are part of the federal government's infrastructure for supporting veterans. Transmitting reports to them is an internal administrative action, not consultation with an outside party before a decision. Furthermore, the report is sent to Congress (inside government). There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or private entities before making a decision.
